speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to your consultation. I am Dr. Agent; to help you, I need to start by asking: What specific symptoms is your neonate experiencing, and how have they changed since birth?

speaker: Patient
text: 1100-g (2-lb 7-oz) newborn, 31 weeks' gestation. The patient was born three days ago with a birth weight of 1100 g at 31 weeks' gestation. The antenatal period was complicated by chorioamnionitis. Apgar scores were 3 and 6 at 1 and 5 minutes, respectively. The patient has become increasingly lethargic over the past 18 hours and experienced a tonic seizure lasting for 25 seconds.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the history. Given the chorioamnionitis, low birth weight, and Apgar scores, is there any history of maternal fever, rupture of membranes, or known GBS colonization? Also, has the infant received any antibiotics or glucose since birth?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Tonic seizure lasting for 25 seconds. I also have Increasing lethargy over the past 18 hours, Appears ill.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Neonatal Sepsis (likely GBS or Polymicrobial) secondary to Chorioamnionitis.

REQUEST TEST: CBC with differential, Blood Culture, CSF Analysis & Gram Stain, Blood Glucose.
REQUEST IMAGES: Head Ultrasound to rule out intraventricular hemorrhage.
